blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Paleolithic Age (Old Stone Age) represents the earliest period of human history, spanning from roughly 2 million years ago to 10,000 BC.
Paleolithic humans led a nomadic lifestyle as hunter-gatherers, relying entirely on wild plants, hunting, and fishing without knowledge of agriculture or permanent housing.
Tools were made of unpolished, rough stone (quartzite), earning these early humans the name 'Quartzite Men' in Indian history.
The accidental discovery of fire was a pivotal turning point, providing protection from predators, warmth during the Ice Age, and a means to cook food.
The era is sub-divided into Lower, Middle, and Upper Paleolithic phases based on the evolution of stone tool technology and climate changes.

blocks.content: Paleolithic humans relied entirely on nature, living as nomadic hunter-gatherers using unpolished, rough stone tools.

rows: Covers the Ice Age; major sites include Soan Valley (Pakistan) and Attirampakkam (Tamil Nadu).
Characterized by Nevasan tool culture; major sites include Luni Valley (Rajasthan) and Narmada Valley.
Coincides with the emergence of Homo sapiens; key sites include Bhimbetka (MP) and Kurnool Caves (AP).

items: Robert Bruce Foote discovered the first Paleolithic stone tool (a handaxe) in India at Pallavaram near Chennai in 1863.
Bhimbetka rock shelters in Madhya Pradesh feature prehistoric cave art and were declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2003.
The 'Narmada Man' fossil found at Hathnora (Madhya Pradesh) is the only known human fossil from the Paleolithic Age in India.
Traces of ash found in Kurnool Caves (Andhra Pradesh) indicate the early domestic use of fire during the Paleolithic period.
